hook.line: Hernando needs a favor from a city office, and a blunt *Vengo a exigir* is a poor way to start. In Spanish, politeness often lives in the tense: you ask in the imperfect.
hook.es: Venía a ver si me podían atender.
hook.en: I was wondering if someone could see me.

examples.es: Venía a ver si me podían atender.
examples.en: I was wondering if someone could see me.

examples.es: Le escribía para preguntar por mi solicitud.
examples.en: I was writing to ask about my application. (formal)

examples.es: Venía a pedirle un favor, don Hernando.
examples.en: I was hoping to ask you a favor, Don Hernando. (formal)

examples.es: Te llamaba para saber si puedes venir mañana.

examples.en: I was calling to find out whether my package has arrived. (formal)

rule:
When you walk up to someone and ask for something, the present tense (*Vengo a pedirle…*) can sound like a demand. The imperfect steps back a little: *Venía a…*, *Le escribía para…*, *Te llamaba para…*.

It still means now. Nothing happened in the past; the tense just makes you sound modest. English does it with *I was wondering if…*

The frame is *venía a* or *llamaba para* plus an infinitive, often followed by *ver si* and a second imperfect: *me podían atender*.

It works best for asking. When you need to sound firm, the present is clearer: *Vengo a decirle que no voy a vender.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this the imperfect of courtesy: the imperfect used for a request in the present, to soften it.

options: I am writing, plainly, to ask for an appointment.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *Vengo* or *Venía* to ask softly: ___ a ver si me podían atender. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Venía a ver si me podían atender.
yourTurn.why: Asking softly takes the imperfect: it steps back from the request.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *escribo* or *escribía* to open a polite letter: Le ___ para preguntar por mi solicitud. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Le escribía para preguntar por mi solicitud.
yourTurn.why: *Escribía* is the modest version of the same request.

yourTurn.prompt: I was hoping to ask you a favor, Don Hernando. (formal)
yourTurn.answer: Venía a pedirle un favor, don Hernando.
yourTurn.why: *Venía a* plus an infinitive is the polite way to say what you came for.

yourTurn.prompt: I was calling to find out if you can come tomorrow. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Te llamaba para saber si puedes venir mañana.
yourTurn.why: A friend is *te*, and *llamaba para* is the soft opening.

yourTurn.prompt: We were hoping to ask about the price of the premises.
yourTurn.answer: Veníamos a preguntar por el precio del local.
yourTurn.why: *Veníamos* is the *we* form, and *preguntar por* asks about something.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it polite with the imperfect: *Vengo a ver si hay mesa.*
yourTurn.answer: Venía a ver si había mesa.
accept: Venía a ver si había una mesa.

yourTurn.prompt: Now say it to a friend: *Le llamaba para saber si ya llegó mi paquete.*
yourTurn.answer: Te llamaba para saber si ya llegó mi paquete.
yourTurn.why: *Le* is for a formal *you*; a friend gets *te*.

pitfalls.wrong: Vine a ver si me podían atender.
pitfalls.right: Venía a ver si me podían atender.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Vine* says you came and that is over; the polite ask needs *venía*, which keeps the request open.
*Querer* takes the infinitive straight away; only *venir* needs the *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Le escribía a preguntar por mi solicitud.
pitfalls.right: Le escribía para preguntar por mi solicitud.
pitfalls.why: *Escribir* takes *para* before the purpose; *venir* is the one that takes *a*.

personal: Think of something you would have to ask a stranger politely, like a table, an appointment or a price. Say it with *Venía a…* or *Te llamaba para…*.
